references.text: The psalm describes how the one who acts righteously and walks in integrity will dwell on the Lord's holy mountain, reflecting the idea of living in holiness and righteousness before God.
These verses speak of the one who walks righteously and speaks what is right, who will dwell in high places—a picture resembling life in holiness and righteousness before God.
Jeremiah speaks of doing what is right and just, which aligns with living in holiness and righteousness before God.
In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus speaks of those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled, echoing the idea of living righteously before God.
Jesus teaches that one's righteousness must surpass that of the scribes and Pharisees to enter the kingdom of heaven, pointing toward a life of holiness and righteousness before God.
Paul urges believers to put on the new self, created after God in true righteousness and holiness, directly reflecting the concept in Luke 1:75.
James speaks of the fruit of righteousness sown in peace by those who make peace, which can be seen in connection with living in righteousness and holiness.
